chapter: Hurry On Down, Capitol and New York
title: Deciding to go to New York and Carlos Gastel becomes manager
summary: After twelve years working for little, she worried about her son, agreed to eight weeks at Cafe Society, and Dexter got Carlos Gastel and GAC to manage her.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So finally, when I did -- when Mr. Josephson talked to me and said, "Nellie, you've got to come to New York," I said, "Well, I'll have to let you know." And I told him about

my little boy. I said, "You know, I have a little son, and I've just, you know, I've got to be sure that my son's going to be taken care of if I go." And he said, "Well, you've got to come to New York, because your record is hot."

This record, I think we did this session in March or April, I think. I can't remember exactly now, of '47. And of course it takes it about three months, I imagine, to really hit, you know, for the impact, because it's released in the east before it's hit here.

So I thought about it and I thought about it, and in the back of my mind I thought, well, now, how in the world can I afford to go to New York. Well, the money really that Mr. Josephson was offering wasn't much, you know, and I got to thinking to myself, now, I can't go to New York and live with that little money. But Mr. Dexter was saying, "Well, I think you should go and try it and see what happens, because you'll be able to make other contacts." In the meantime, he says, "I'm going to talk to Carlos Gastel , because what you really need is a good manager. You need a good, good manager and a good agent." I didn't have either one.

And sure enough, he did talk to Carlos Gastel and GAC, and of course Carlos worked very closely with GAC, you know, because he had Nat, Peggy Lee, Mel Torme, Stan Kenton, all of these people were GAC. So anyway, he talked to Mr. Gastel and got him interested in me, and well, it just started,

it just happened that way. However, I did agree to go to New York and work for Barney Josephson for the first, you know, for eight weeks at least. So after that time, then Carlos Gastel took over as my manager, and that's when things began to happen.
I worked theaters, nightclubs, and I continued to record, you know.
